events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The dispute is entered through NS-0: the cancellation was by the driver, and the driver's cancellation was on the ground of rider no-show, so the case is governed by NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F12][NS-0]. The charge in dispute is the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F8].

NS-1 requires all three conditions, and each is documented by system records. (i) Arrival confirmation: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:18:50 [F6], which is corroborated by the chat message at 17:19 ("I'm here at the pickup point") [F10]. (ii) Location at the moment of the tap: GPS puts the driver 38 m from the pickup when the tap was made, well inside the 200 m arrival radius, and his closest approach over the whole wait was 34 m [F6][F1][NS-1]. (iii) Waiting time: after the tap the driver stayed continuously within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (220 s) until cancelling at 17:22:30, i.e. more than 3 minutes [F6][F3][F4][NS-1]; the platform's own timeline likewise records arrival at 17:17:50 and cancellation 4 min 40 s later [F5], and the driver's chat at 17:22 confirms he had waited more than 3 minutes [F11][F12].

Because all of NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid and no refund is due under NS-2, whose precondition is that one of those conditions fails [NS-2]. The rider's explanation that she came out "a minute" after the cancellation does not displace the requirement: the fee attaches to the rider not arriving at the pickup point within the 3-minute wait after the driver's confirmed arrival, which the timeline shows did not happen [F5][F6][NS-1]. RydeTAXI rules on metered waiting units are irrelevant here; this is a fixed-quote RydeX booking [F4][RD-3].

Two record conflicts exist and are resolved in the driver's favour by the system-record rule: the timeline field F7 states the driver never tapped "I'm Here", while F6 and F5 record a tap at 17:18:50 and a platform arrival at 17:17:50; the corroborating chat at 17:19 [F10] supports F6/F5, so the tap and arrival are treated as established [F5][F6][F10][NS-1]. Traffic and weather facts are neutral and point to no alternative explanation for the driver's wait [F13][F14][F15].

No account action is warranted: NS-2's flag_account branch applies only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, which is not the case here (38 m at the tap, 34 m closest) [F1][F6][NS-2]. The driver's profile shows two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days [F17], but the profile is not a basis for adjudicating this case and this case is not an upheld deviation, so RD-6 is not triggered [F17][RD-6].
